## 2

I understand being skeptical of official narratives and digital media, but the evidence for a spherical Earth doesn't depend on NASA or satellite photos. You can test it yourself using basic geometry. For instance, watch ships disappear over the horizon hull-first, observe how entirely different constellations appear as you travel between the northern and southern hemispheres, or look at the Earth's shadow during a lunar eclipse—it is always an arc, which only a sphere can produce from every angle. A flat model simply cannot explain all of these everyday observations at once.

## 3

Sunlight looks white, but it’s actually made of all the colors of the rainbow mixed together. You can think of each color as a wave: reds and oranges have long, lazy waves, while blues and purples have short, choppy waves. 

Our atmosphere is full of gas molecules like nitrogen and oxygen. When sunlight hits the atmosphere, the long red waves pass right through without hitting much. But the short, choppy blue waves collide with those gas molecules and bounce around in every direction. This is called Rayleigh scattering. When you look up away from the Sun, your eyes are catching that scattered blue light bouncing around the sky.

夜色渐深，窗外的细雨不紧不慢地下着，在玻璃上汇成一道道交错的水痕。昏黄的路灯被水汽晕开，模糊成一个个微弱的光圈。街道空空荡荡，偶尔有车辆驶过，轮胎碾过积水，带起一阵清脆的水花声。空气里弥漫着潮湿的泥土与植物气息。听着屋檐下断断续续的滴答声，白日里的喧嚣退去，整个世界似乎都安静了下来。
